authority_boundary: This independent receipt supports only conceptual-depth and understanding-gain gates for a conjectural research programme. It does not validate any source claim, mathematical premise, continuum construction, universality theorem, or Yang--Mills mass gap.

distinctions: Scale production answers why a positive number appears; observable completeness answers whether it controls every relevant physical mode; descent stability answers whether that meaning survives presentation change.
Regulator refinement, continuum passage, OS reconstruction, and unitary representation comparison remain distinct arrow types.
Theory identity, nontriviality, and a positive spectral lower bound remain distinct conclusions.

assumptions: The same physical Yang-Mills theory is a coherent descent class of presentations, not an unexamined identity of their local carriers.
A physical mass scale is neither a bare finite-cutoff number nor a detector-relative correlation length; it is a produced, detected, and stably descended invariant.
The three witnesses are jointly necessary within this programme and none may be defined by the desired Hamiltonian conclusion.
unresolved_contradictions: It remains unknown whether a noncircular arrow class broad enough for four-dimensional Yang-Mills admits cutoff-uniform distortion and vanishing holonomy; the live dissent is that continuum identity may be local/algebraic without any globally coherent spectral-scale cocycle.

correction_conditions: YM21-C01: Reject the mediator if an admissible arrow is defined by preserving the mass gap or by assuming the target continuum theory.
YM21-C02: Split or demote the scale component if volume-uniform coercivity fails to control lattice-spacing removal in physical units.
YM21-C03: Reject the observable component if its detector family has a nontrivial kernel on any target-relevant nonvacuum sector.
YM21-C04: Abandon regulator-independent synthesis if comparison-loop holonomy remains nonzero or path dependent at the continuum limit.
YM21-C05: Revise the ontology if groupoid language adds no independently checkable law beyond listing the original missing lemmas.

YM21-C06: Retire the programme if it cannot recover established reflection-positive finite-regulator results without changing the Clay target's dimension, gauge-group scope, nontriviality, or Hamiltonian meaning.

counterfactuals: A uniform lattice scale with a nonconservative observable core leaves hidden nonvacuum modes and does not establish the physical gap.
A complete observable core with a scale that vanishes along cutoff removal has no positive continuum gap to detect.
Positive local scales and complete detectors with path-dependent transport do not identify one regulator-independent Yang-Mills theory.

new_questions: Which minimal independent axioms on scale production, detector conservativity, and arrow coherence imply a positive regulator-independent Hamiltonian spectral lower bound without defining any axiom by that conclusion?
Can one construct a finite countermodel with a positive scale cocycle but a nonconservative observable detector?
Which regulator-comparison loops expose nonuniversality through a nonvanishing transport holonomy defect?
Does an AQFT recovery or nuclearity condition supply exactly the detector conservativity needed after OS reconstruction?
Can the conditional F09 theorem be proved before any full Yang-Mills construction, thereby testing whether the mediator has real mathematical content?

obligations.tests: YM21-F01: Define the spectral-descent transport groupoid: regulated reflection-positive Yang-Mills presentations as objects; refinement, comparison, continuum, and OS maps as typed arrows; identities, domains, and composition must be stated without a mass-gap premise.

YM21-F02: Define a dimensionful scale-production witness kappa(P) from coercive, Poincare, transfer, or clustering data and state volume, lattice-spacing, coupling, and physical-unit quantifiers explicitly.
YM21-F03: Define a gauge-invariant observable detector functor O(P) and an exact conservativity/density condition on the OS reconstructed nonvacuum Hilbert sector.
YM21-F04: Prove or refute a recovery theorem connecting Euclidean detector correlations to the full Hamiltonian spectral measure, including superselection and hidden-mode boundary cases.
YM21-F05: Define arrow distortion D(f) for the scale witness and prove kappa(Q) >= D(f) kappa(P), with a nonvacuous composition inequality for D(g composed with f).
YM21-F06: Define transport of observable semantics along each arrow type and prove compatibility with reflection positivity, quotienting null states, and OS time evolution.
YM21-F07: Define descent stability as path independence or a quantitatively vanishing holonomy defect on regulator-comparison loops, with cutoff-uniform rates and no post hoc admissibility.
YM21-F08: Prove continuum identity and nontriviality for the descended object independently of the scale witness, distinguishing equivalence of selected observables from equivalence of theories.

YM21-F09: Prove a conditional spectral-descent theorem and three independence countermodels: positive scale with incomplete detectors; complete detectors with vanishing scale; and both local witnesses with unstable/path-dependent descent.

risk_reward.mechanism_path: A spectral-descent transport groupoid factors any proposed lattice-to-continuum mass-gap argument into three separately falsifiable witnesses: a noncircular coercive mechanism that produces a dimensionful candidate scale on each regulated presentation; a conservative gauge-invariant observable family that detects the reconstructed nonvacuum spectrum; and a descent-stability law showing that scale and observable semantics compose coherently across independently defined regulator, continuum, and representation arrows. Only their conjunction could license a presentation-independent spectral conclusion.

scope_conditions: positive Hamiltonian spectral gap above the vacuum

source_relation_assessments.reason: The volume-uniform coercivity claim sharpens scale production while leaving continuum descent and observable completeness separate.
Its claim bundle collides with transfer, clustering, universality, and OS burdens without independently validating the mediator.
AQFT observable completeness motivates the detector condition but does not supply scale production or regulator descent.

understanding_delta.after: Mass-gap transfer is a factorized descent problem requiring three non-substitutable witnesses: scale production, observable completeness, and descent stability; each has a distinct countermodel and formal burden.
understanding_delta.before: Coercivity, Euclidean clustering, OS reconstruction, universality, and the Hamiltonian gap appeared as one long bridge, so a failure could be moved between steps without locating the conceptual defect.

preserved_differences: Coercive scale production does not prove observable completeness.
Observable completeness does not produce a positive scale.
Descent coherence neither produces the scale nor proves detector conservativity.
OS reconstruction is not regulator universality.
Agreement of selected observables is not full theory identity or nontriviality.
A vanishing holonomy defect is a transport condition, not a proof of a positive Hamiltonian lower bound.
